Rashi on Nedarim 10a:10:1.hebrew: והדין קרא בנזיר טמא כתיב - על שם שטימא את עצמו במת, קאמר קרא אשר חטא על הנפש:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:10:1.english: And this verse is written with regard to a ritually impure nazirite - [It is] on account of [the fact] that he rendered himself ritually impure with a corpse [that] the verse states, "for he sinned against the soul."

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:10:2.hebrew: משום דשנה בחטא הוא - דעל שם ששנה עצמו בחטא, שנזר עצמו, ועוד שטימא נזירותו, להכי כתיב ביה "אשר חטא על הנפש". והוא הדין נמי לשאר נזירין דאיקרו חוטאים, וגלי רחמנא בהאי והוא הדין לכולהו. ואהכי גילה בהאי, משום דזה שונה בחטא שני פעמים, ותולין הקלקלה במקולקל:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:10:2.english: Because he repeated a sin - For because he repeated himself in sin — [in] that he made himself a nazirite, and furthermore that he defiled his naziriteship — therefore it is written concerning him, "for he sinned regarding the soul." And the same law applies also to other nazirites, that they are called sinners; the Merciful One revealed [it] in this [case], and the same law applies to all of them. And for this reason [Scripture] revealed [it] in this [case]: because this one repeats a sin twice, and we attribute corruption to the corrupt.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:11:1.english: One who says konam - That he said, "Konam [be] this loaf upon me."

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:11:2.hebrew: חרק - האומר ככר זה עליך חרק. או שאמר נזיק, נזיח, פזיח — הריני נזיק אם אוכל ככר זה, או שאמר נזיח — הוי כאילו נדר בנזיר:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:11:2.english: Ḥerek - [That is,] one who says, "This loaf is ḥerek to you." Or [in the case of] one who said nazik, naziaḥ, [or] paziaḥ — [for example,] "I am a nazik if I eat this loaf," or who said naziaḥ — it is as though he took a vow of naziriteship.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:11:3.hebrew: שבותה - שלא אוכל ככר זה, או שקוקה, הרי אלו כינווים לשבועה, והוי כאילו נשבע ממש:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:11:3.english: Shevuta - [E.g., "Shevuta] that I will not eat this loaf," or "shekuka," these are substitutes for an oath, and it is as if he actually swore.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:11:4.hebrew: נדיר במוהי - כמו מומתא, לשון שבועה:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:11:4.english: [One who] vows with [the term] mohi - Like mometa, [which is] an expression of an oath.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:12:1.english: It was stated [regarding] substitutes - that [the Tanna] teaches in the Mishnah.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:12:2.hebrew: רבי יוחנן אמר לשון אומות הן - דהכי משתבעי אומות, וכי נדרי אז משתבעי משתעו בהני לשונות. וישראל נמי, כי אמר בהאי לישנא מיתסר, דהתורה אמרה כי ידור — בכל לשון דנדר:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:12:2.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They are a language of [other] nations - For thus the nations swear; and when they vow, then [when] they swear, they speak in these languages. And a Jew as well, when he speaks in this language, becomes prohibited [by his vow], for the Torah stated, "When [a man] vows" — [meaning] in any language of vowing.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:12:3.english: Language that the Sages devised for them - The Sages invented these expressions for them so that they would vow with them.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:13:1.hebrew: תקינו חכמים כינויין דלא לימא קרבן - בשם, כדאמרינן בעלמא (עירובין ד' כא:): קודם שבא שלמה היתה תורה דומה לכפיפה שאין לה אזנים, עד שבא שלמה ותיקן לה אזנים, דכתיב: איזן וחיקר תיקן משלים הרבה, שגזר על השניות כי היכי דלא לפגעו באיסורא דאורייתא. הכי נמי תקינו רבנן כינויין לנדרים, דהנודר בהני כינויין כאילו נודר בקרבן עצמו, וכן בכינוי דחרם. וכגון נמי: ושמרתם את משמרתי (ויקרא י״ח:ל׳) — עשו משמרת למשמרתי — כי היכי דלא ליתי למינדר בנדר דאורייתא, דאתי למימר נמי קרבן לה'. והיינו דתנן (אבות פ"ג מי"ג): נדרים סיג לפרישות, שתיקנו אלו כינויין כדי להפריש האדם מן העבירה:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:13:1.english: The Sages established substitutes so that one not say "offering" - [i.e.,] with the [Divine] Name, as we say elsewhere (Eruvin 21b): Before Solomon came, the Torah was like a basket without handles, until Solomon came and made handles for it, as it is written: "He pondered, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs" — for he decreed regarding secondary [prohibited relationships] so that [people] would not come to transgress a biblical prohibition. So too, the Sages established substitutes for vows, [such] that one who vows with these substitutes is as if he vows by an offering itself, and likewise with a substitute for cherem [a vow of consecration]. And similarly, [as is derived from] "And you shall keep My charge" (Leviticus 18:30) — make a safeguard for My charge — so that one not come to vow with a biblical vow, [whereby] he might also come to say "an offering to the Lord." And this is what we learned [in the Mishnah] (Avot 3:13): "Vows are a fence for abstinence," for they established these substitutes in order to keep a person away from transgression.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:1:1.hebrew: אפילו תימא רבי יהודה היא - מתני' דשני בין נדר לנדבה, דלר' יהודה נמי שאני ליה. וכי קאמר ר' יהודה "טוב נודר ומשלם", היינו דאמר בלשון נדבה, אבל בנדר לא אמר:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:1:1.english: Even if you say it is Rabbi Yehuda - [that is,] the Mishnah that distinguishes between a vow and a gift [offering], for according to Rabbi Yehuda as well, there is a distinction [between them]; and when Rabbi Yehuda said, "Good is one who vows and pays," that is [only] when one spoke in the language of a gift [offering], but with a vow he did not say [so].

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:3:1.hebrew: מ"ש נדר דלא כו' דאתי בה לידי תקלה - כדלעיל:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:3:1.english: What is different [about] a vow, that [one should] not [make one], etc., that he may come through it to a stumbling block - As [explained] above.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:6:1.hebrew: לפי שאין הקב"ה מביא תקלה על ידייהן - (שאין באין) כלומר, שהם מתייראים שלא יעשו שום חטא, ורוצין להביא קרבן להתכפר עליהם. לפי שאין הקב"ה מביא תקלה על ידיהם, מה היו עושין כדי שיתחייבו קרבן? שאין מביאין קרבן חטאת אלא על חטא ממש. ענין אחר: לפי שאין הקב"ה מביא תקלה על ידיהם — שאין באין לידי שום תקלה ושום חטא שיתחייבו קרבן חטאת:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:6:1.english: Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not bring about a stumbling block through them - (that they do not come) That is to say, they are afraid lest they commit some sin, and they wish to bring an offering to atone for themselves. [Therefore,] because the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not bring about a stumbling block through them, what would they do in order to become obligated [to bring] an offering? For one does not bring a sin-offering except for an actual sin. Another explanation: "Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, does not bring about a stumbling block through them" — [meaning] that they do not come to any stumbling block or any sin for which they would be obligated [to bring] a sin-offering.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:7:1.hebrew: אלא הרוצה להתנדב מתנדב ומביא שלמים וכו' - אבל חטאת לא אתי בנדבה, ובנזירות נמי לא היו מתנדבין שלא יקראו חוטאים. ומתני' דקתני נדר בנזיר, דמשמע דכשרים נודרין בנזירות, לאו ר' שמעון היא:
Rashi on Nedarim 10a:7:1.english: Rather, one who wants to volunteer volunteers and brings a peace-offering, etc. - However, a sin-offering does not come as a voluntary offering, and they also did not volunteer naziriteship so that they would not be called sinners. And the Mishnah, which teaches [the case of one who] vowed [to be] a nazirite — which implies that righteous [people] vow naziriteship — is not [the view of] Rabbi Shimon.

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:8:1.english: All of them [are of] one opinion - That they align their opinions in one line [of reasoning].

Rashi on Nedarim 10a:8:2.english: That a nazirite is a sinner - Because he vowed.

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:10:1.hebrew: דשנה בחטא - בצער של יין, כי חוזר ומתחיל נזירות; אי נמי: שנה בחטא דיין ובטומאה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:10:1.english: Because he repeated [his] sin - [That is,] in the distress of [abstaining from] wine, when he goes back and begins [his] naziriteship [anew]; alternatively, he repeated [sinning] with the sin of wine and with [the sin of] ritual impurity.

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:11:1.hebrew: חרק חרך וכו' - אין לפרש משום דלשונות הללו נוטין קצת אחר לשון חרם, אלא למאן דאמר לשון אומות נינהו דוקא; [אבל] למ"ד לשון שבדו חכמים — [לא, דא"כ לתני נמי חרך חרט]:
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:11:1.english: Ḥerek, ḥerekh, etc. - One should not explain [that these are valid substitutes] because these terms incline somewhat toward the term ḥerem, except specifically according to the one who says [that] they are languages of the nations; [but] according to the one who says [that they are] a language that the Sages coined — [no, for if so, let it also teach ḥerekh, ḥeret].

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:12:1.hebrew: וכן הוא אומר בחדש אשר בדא מלבו - וכה"ג לא אשכחן בעלמא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:12:1.english: And so it states: "In the month that he had devised in his own heart" - And we do not find [anything] like this elsewhere.

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:13:1.hebrew: ה"ג: דלא לימא קרבן. ולימא קרבן? דלמא אמר קרבן לה'. ונימא קרבן לה'? דילמא אמר לה' ולא אמר קרבן - והאי טעמא שייך בכולהו [כמו] בנדרים, כדאמר הש"ס: בנזיר — דלא לימא "לה' הריני נזיר", כדכתיב "נזיר להזיר לה'" (במדבר ו׳:ב׳); וחרם — דלא לימא "לה' חרם", דכתיב "אשר יחרם איש לה'" (ויקרא כ״ז:כ״ח); וכן שבועה — דכתיב "שבועת ה' תהיה וגו'" (שמות כ״ב:י׳). ומשום דעיקר מכילתין בנדרים, נקט לפרושי הכי בנדרים דוקא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:13:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "So that one not say 'offering' (korban). And let him say 'offering'! Perhaps he will say 'an offering to the Lord.' And let him say 'an offering to the Lord'! Perhaps he will say 'to the Lord' and not say 'offering'" - And this reason applies to all of them [just as] to vows, as the Talmud states: with a nazirite — so that he not say, "To the Lord, I am hereby a nazirite," as it is written, "a nazirite to consecrate himself to the Lord" (Numbers 6:2); and [with] a cherem — so that he not say, "To the Lord, [this is] cherem," as it is written, "anything that a man devotes to the Lord" (Leviticus 27:28); and similarly [with] an oath — as it is written, "the oath of the Lord shall be, etc." (Exodus 22:10). And because the primary [focus] of our tractate is vows, [the Gemara] chose to explain this specifically with regard to vows.

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:1:1.hebrew: <abbr title="ואי בעית אימא">ואבע"א</abbr>: כי קאמר <abbr title="רבי">ר'</abbr> יהודה בנדר, אבל בנדבה לא קאמר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:1:1.english: And if you wish, say: When Rabbi Yehuda said [it], [he said it] with regard to a vow, but with regard to a gift offering he did not say [it].

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:3:1.hebrew: נדבה נמי אתי לידי תקלה - ומשני: "ר"י לטעמיה". ה"מ לשנויי כדלעיל, אלא ניחא ליה לאתויי כרבי יהודה גופיה. וכן בסמוך [גבי] נזירות, מייתי מר' יהודה "חסידים הראשונים וכו'" מהאי טעמא, אע"ג דהוה מצי לשנויי כדלעיל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:3:1.english: A gift [offering] also [has the concern that] he may encounter a stumbling block - And [the Gemara] answers: "Rabbi Yehuda [conforms] to his [own] reasoning." It could have answered as [it did] above, but it prefers to cite Rabbi Yehuda himself. And similarly, immediately below regarding naziriteship, it cites from Rabbi Yehuda [the statement about] "the early pious ones, etc." for this [same] reason, even though it could have answered as [it did] above.

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:4:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה אומר אדם מביא כבשתו בעזרה - ואם תאמר: וללישנא קמא דאוקמינא פלוגתייהו בנדר, ואפי' בנדר שרי ר' יהודה, הא דקתני בהו "אדם מביא כבשתו וכו'", אלמא חייש רבי יהודה לתקלה, ואפי' בנדבה לא שרי אלא בכה"ג, לכ"ש בנדר דמיתסר? וי"ל דאיכא למימר עצה טובה קמ"ל. וא"ת: והא בתוספתא קתני "ר' יהודה אמר טוב מזה ומזה", ש"מ דלענין איסורא קאמר? וי"ל דלעולם עצה טובה קמ"ל הך ברייתא, ולא משום איסורא קאמר; ואיידי דאיירי ר"מ "טוב מזה ומזה", דלענין איסור קאמר ר"מ, א"ר יהודה נמי האי לישנא "טוב מזה ומזה", ולעולם לענין עצה טובה קמ"ל, ולא לענין איסור קא"ל. והשתא מסיק לישנא בתרא דנדרים אתי לכ"ע אפי' לר' יהודה, וכן ללישנא קמא אפי' לר"מ בנדבה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:4:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: A person brings his lamb into the Courtyard - And if you say: According to the first version [of the Gemara], where we established their dispute as concerning a neder [vow], and even in the case of a neder Rabbi Yehuda permits [vowing] — [consider] that which is taught regarding them, "A person brings his lamb, etc.," which shows that Rabbi Yehuda is concerned about a stumbling block, and even in the case of a nedavah [freewill offering] he only permits it in such a manner; is it not all the more so in the case of a neder that it should be forbidden? One can say that it is possible to say [that] he is teaching us good advice. And if you say: But in the Tosefta it teaches, "Rabbi Yehuda says: Better than this one and that one [is one who does not vow at all]," which implies that he is speaking with respect to a prohibition? One can say that in truth this baraita is teaching us good advice, and he is not speaking because of a prohibition; rather, since Rabbi Meir used [the expression] "Better than this one and that one" — as Rabbi Meir was speaking with respect to a prohibition — Rabbi Yehuda also used this expression, "Better than this one and that one," yet in truth he is teaching us [this] with respect to good advice, and is not saying it with respect to a prohibition. And now, [the Gemara] concludes [according to] the latter version that [the case of] nedarim accords with everyone, even Rabbi Yehuda, and similarly according to the first version, [it accords] even with Rabbi Meir with respect to a nedavah.

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:4:2.hebrew: אדם מביא כבשתו - מדנקט לשון נקיבה, אלמא דבשלמים איירי. ותימה: דמאי תקלה שייך בשלמים? והלא אין מעילה בשלמים! וי"ל: דנהי דמעילה ליכא, איסור דאורייתא מיהא איכא, כדאמר בר"ה (דף כח -): בשופר של שלמים לא יתקע, ואם תקע לא יצא, משום דאיסורא רכיב עליה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:4:2.english: A person brings his lamb [kivsato] - Since [the baraita] uses the feminine form, it is evident that it is speaking of a peace-offering [shelamim]. And this is astonishing: what stumbling block is relevant to a peace-offering — after all, there is no misuse of consecrated property [me'ilah] with a peace-offering! And one can answer: Although there is no me'ilah, there is nevertheless a Torah prohibition, as [the Gemara] says in Rosh Hashanah (28a): With a shofar of a peace-offering one may not blow, and if he blew [it] he has not fulfilled [his obligation], because a prohibition rests upon it.

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:8:1.hebrew: אמר אביי שמעון הצדיק כו' - תרוייהו אינם שוין: ר"ש איירי בנזיר טמא כדאמר לעיל, ור' אליעזר הקפר איירי בטהור? וי"ל דאה"נ, ולהכי לא קאמר "דבר אחד" אלא "שיטה א'", דכולהו ס"ל דנזיר חוטא טפי מרבנן דידהו; וכה"ג אמרי' בהמוכר את הספינה (דף עח:):
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:8:1.english: Abaye said: Shimon HaTzaddik, etc. - [Surely] the two of them are not alike: Rabbi Shimon is speaking of an impure nazirite, as he said above, whereas Rabbi Eliezer HaKappar is speaking of a pure [nazirite]? And one can say that indeed it is so, and for this reason [Abaye] does not say "the same thing" [davar echad], but rather "one approach" [shitah achat], for all of them hold that a nazirite is a sinner, more so than their [disputing] Rabbis; and similarly we say in [the chapter] HaMokher Et HaSefinah ([Bava Batra] 78b).

Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:8:2.hebrew: כולן שיטה אחת הן - לאו דוקא, שהרי שמעון הצדיק אין להוכיח, דטעמא אינו אלא מפני שמתחרטין. וכה״ג איכא בפרק רבן גמליאל (יבמות דף נא: ושם): "כולהו סבירא להו מאמר קונה קנין גמור". הר״ר יוסף זצ״ל כדפירש':
Tosafot on Nedarim 10a:8:2.english: They are all of the same opinion - [This is] not exact, for [regarding] Shimon HaTzaddik, one cannot prove [that he holds a nazirite is a sinner], since [his] reason is only because they regret [their vows]. And similarly there is [such an expression] in the chapter Rabban Gamliel (Yevamot 51b and elsewhere): "They all hold that ma'amar effects a complete acquisition." [So stated] Rabbi Yosef, of blessed memory, as he explained.
